title: Creating our illustrations
slide_intent: Teach designers how to extend an illustration family when the subject is new. Shared construction rules let different drawings retain a recognizable outline at the sizes where readers encounter them.
strategic_value: Frontline AIDS can depict a missing subject with colors appropriate to it while keeping the line weight and footprint consistent with existing illustrations.
demonstration: A gridded pink heart makes the outline and safe zone visible. The guide specifies a 31-square grid, one pixel per square, a one-square outline and a maximum of three colors. A separate size comparison labels the minimum height as 70 px.
practical_value: Construct a new shape on the supplied grid with a one-square outline. Limit the palette to three colors, then check the illustration’s minimum height before counting any added sticker border.

content_islands.name: Section rail and introduction
content_islands.spec: Mark Creating our illustrations in the rail. Place the two-line heading and introductory copy at upper left. Explain when to draw a new image, how to limit its colors and when a containing circle is appropriate.

content_islands.name: Construction notes
content_islands.spec: Align a narrow column of three notes beside the introduction. Distinguish the grid unit, outline thickness and use of additional colors for context.

content_islands.name: Grid specimen
content_islands.spec: Give the right half to a pink heart with a black edge on a fine blue square grid. Frame the whole specimen and point to the safe zone outside the inner grid.

content_islands.name: Minimum-height comparison
content_islands.spec: Align the small examples along a common baseline beneath the grid. Mark the 70 px minimum height and attach the pink note about measuring the original art when adding a sticker edge.
